title: Table 1 Characteristics by recorded gestational hypertension or preeclampsia

title: Table 2 Overall standardized risks and associations
note: HC0 covariance. Each block has one reference group: SS in the primary model and S in the before-pregnancy model. The primary model is one logistic model of the three groups with group-specific age splines; the three standardized risks share the covariate distribution of the pooled SS, SN and NN complete cases, so they are on one absolute scale. The before-pregnancy block is standardized to its own complete cases. The two populations overlap. SS: women who smoked before pregnancy and in the first trimester; SN: women who smoked before pregnancy and reported none in the first trimester; NN: women who reported none in either period; S: any smoking before pregnancy; N: none before pregnancy, irrespective of the first trimester. title: Table S5. Crossover ages, local 95% confidence intervals, null-age confidence sets and simultaneous sign regions, all GH/PE specifications
note: Local implicit-delta intervals with HC0 covariance, conditional on a regular fitted root; they are not whole-zero-set confidence sets and do not establish uniqueness. The null-age confidence set is the whole 95% set from inverting the pointwise band. Opposite directions refers to simultaneous-band evidence on the two sides of the displayed crossover. Every row names one group first and its reference second, and the last three columns describe the first-named group relative to that reference. The first two rows are the primary model, whose reference is SS (protocol addendum K); the third is the supplementary SN vs NN contrast of the same fit, whose reference is NN; the fourth is the first-trimester margin, whose exposed arm is smoking in the first trimester. The remaining rows are the released two-arm specifications, each kept in its released orientation with the more-exposed group named first, so the released before-pregnancy fit appears here as S vs N while Table 3 reports that same fit as N vs S. A crossover age and its local interval do not depend on which group is the reference, so every value in the second column is the same in either orientation. The 2014–2015 historical model is retained here; Figure 3 omits it. Models overlap; no across-model multiplicity control is claimed. Simultaneous coverage is across age within each contrast; it is not joint coverage across contrasts.

note: Eight synthetic correctly specified contrast scenarios; 6,000 records per replication; no fit/solver failures or warnings. Monte Carlo intervals are Wilson intervals. title: Table S18 Global and exploratory maternal-age by smoking interaction tests
note: Likelihood-ratio tests compare full and reduced binary logistic models on identical complete cases, with the same spline bases and covariates. Reduced models omit only smoking-by-age terms. HC0 sandwich Wald tests jointly assess the same interaction coefficients as a robustness check. These tests concern interaction on the log-odds model scale; standardized risk ratios and differences remain the reported effect measures. Interaction significance alone does not establish a reversal; direction is assessed separately in Table S19. Holm adjustment covers the two global model hypotheses separately for each test method; the three exploratory contrast-specific tests form a separate family. LRT and Wald results are complementary checks, not independent replication. P values below 0.001 are reported as <0.001; finite log-tail values are retained in the machine-readable results.

note: Crossover ages and local 95% implicit-delta CIs use HC0 covariance.
